newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps- Gas oil edged up on physical.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps- Gas oil edged up on physical.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were firmer at midday on Thursday on higher traded physical levels on Wednesday as buyers returned to the market, brokers said.
"The market picked up slightly as physical buyers came back yesterday," one broker said.
A trader said the physical market will be around Wednesday's levels or a tad firmer today.

The front month gas oil swaps rose slightly to $25.40/$25.60 per barrel from Wednesday's $25.25/$25.35 in very thin trade as players wound down for the Lunar New Year and the Eid-el-Fitri holidays, brokers said.
On the physical market, a 150,000-barrel cargo traded late Wednesday at $25.20 per barrel free-on-board Singapore, up 40 cents from Tuesday's traded level.
Another 150,000-barrel lot was traded between a Singapore trader and a European major at $24.90 a barrel for February 20-24 lifting fob.
Fuel oil swaps extended its recent rally despite agressive physical offers in the face of prompt oversupply, brokers said.
Traders said the firmer swaps market was due to some paper players' belief that cargo prices were under-valued.
Fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $99.50 per tonne with no firm sellers seen against it, up from Wednesday's $99.25/$100.00, brokers said.
